interest: Japanese passport rules, the 1935 redefinition of emigrants and passports for Latin America.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.0128, spanning October 1932 to August 1939) comprises diplomatic despatches, consular correspondence, circular visa instructions, cross-reference sheets, and public inquiries concerning Japanese passport regulations, formats, and procedures. The records document the administrative requirements for Japanese nationals traveling to the United States, successive revisions in Japanese passport design (including bilingual validity clauses, leather bindings, and explicit nationality declarations), and the expansion of three-year multiple-journey passports to Central and South America to support Japanese commercial interests. In addition, the file touches upon diplomatic complexities such as Japanese nationals traveling on 'Manchukuo' passports, student travel to the Philippines, public inquiries regarding consular offices, and a comprehensive comparative survey conducted by the State Department in 1939 that acquired specimen passports representing all categories issued throughout Japan proper and its overseas territories (Korea, Taiwan, Karafuto, Kwantung, and the South Seas Mandate).

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Tokyo Despatch No. 532 regarding passport application requirements for Japanese nationals traveling to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on documents Japanese nationals needed for U.S. passports (Eiichi Murakami case).
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Documents Required for Japanese Nationals Applying for U.S. Passports

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet referencing a Labor Department letter regarding the continuing validity of Japanese passports abroad.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on how long Japanese passports remain valid (Sang Pok Suh case).
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Validity of Japanese Passports

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting the introduction of new Japanese ordinary and special passport forms with bilingual validity statements.
subfiles.summary: Garrels reports new Japanese special and ordinary passport forms with English and French validity statements and sends specimens.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1032: New Form of Japanese Special and Ordinary Passports

subfiles.about: Inquiry from a private citizen in Brockton, Massachusetts, regarding passport requirements for Japan and Korea and Japanese representation in Boston.
subfiles.summary: Myron L. Fuller asks about Japanese and Korean passport rules and whether Japan has a consulate in Boston.
subfiles.title: Letter from Myron L. Fuller Requesting Information on Japanese and Korean Passports

subfiles.about: State Department reply providing circulars on passport application and visa procedures and identifying the Japanese Honorary Consul in Boston.
subfiles.summary: Ruth B. Shipley sends Fuller passport circulars and names Richard Eli Danielson as Japan's honorary consul in Boston.
subfiles.title: Letter to Myron L. Fuller Concerning Passport Procedures and Japanese Representation in Boston

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note transmitting specimen copies of revised Japanese ordinary and special passports to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador sends specimen revised ordinary and special passports.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note from Japanese Ambassador Transmitting Specimen Revised Passports

subfiles.about: Formal diplomatic note acknowledging receipt of specimen revised Japanese passports for reference purposes.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges the Japanese Ambassador's note of June 4, 1935 and keeps the specimen passports.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note to Japanese Ambassador Acknowledging Receipt of Specimen Passports

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting on the revision of Japanese passport regulations and the expansion of multi-journey passports to Latin America.
subfiles.summary: Garrels sends a Foreign Office release on Japan's July 22, 1935 passport revisions, chiefly adding Latin American countries to multi-journey special passports.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1111: Revision of Japanese Passport Regulations

subfiles.about: Japanese Foreign Office press release announcing amendments to passport regulations, travel procedures, and immigrant protection enforcement.
subfiles.summary: Japanese text of the Foreign Office release on 1935 passport revisions: emigrants defined by labor intent, multi-journey passports extended to Latin America, police certification dropped.
subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Office Press Release on Revised Passport Regulations (Japanese Text)

subfiles.about: English translation of the Japanese Foreign Office press release detailing four key revisions to passport regulations and immigrant administration.
subfiles.from: American Consulate General, Tokyo (Translator J. A.)
subfiles.summary: English translation of the July 22, 1935 release: emigrants redefined by labor purpose, three-year passports extended to Latin America, police certification dropped.
subfiles.title: Translation of Japanese Foreign Office Press Release on Revised Passport Regulations

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Tokyo Despatch No. 2279 regarding the Japanese Foreign Office's refusal to issue collective travel documents for students visiting the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew's despatch No. 2279: Japan declined collective travel documents for student groups to the Philippines.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Passports for Japanese Student Groups Traveling to the Philippines

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a despatch from China concerning visa procedures for Japanese nationals presenting Manchukuo passports.
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson (American Ambassador to China)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch No. 374 on visas for a Japanese national (Chuichi Ohashi) holding a Manchukuo passport.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Visa Procedure for Japanese National Presenting Manchukuo Passport

subfiles.about: Letter from Mary E. Gould of Olean, New York, addressed to First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt offering old passport papers in her possession.
subfiles.summary: Mary E. Gould of Olean, New York, writes to First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt concerning historical passport documents in her possession. The White House forwarded the correspondence to the Department of State for appropriate administrative action.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mary E. Gould to Eleanor Roosevelt Offering Passport Papers

subfiles.about: State Department letter acknowledging receipt of a package of historical passport documents forwarded by Mary E. Gould.
subfiles.from: Nathaniel P. Davis (Chief, Division of Foreign Service Administration)
subfiles.summary: Nathaniel P. Davis thanks Mary E. Gould of Olean, New York, for sending the passport papers mentioned in her October 18 letter.
subfiles.title: Letter to Mary E. Gould Acknowledging Receipt of Passport Papers

subfiles.about: Initial State Department communication requesting that Mary E. Gould forward the passport documents she offered in her letter to Mrs. Roosevelt.
subfiles.from: Nathaniel P. Davis (Chief, Division of Foreign Service Administration)
subfiles.summary: Replying for Mrs. Roosevelt, Nathaniel P. Davis asks Mary E. Gould to send the passport and papers to the Department and explain how she obtained them.
subfiles.title: Letter to Mary E. Gould Requesting Delivery of Passport Papers

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch reporting revisions to the Japanese passport form, including a leather cover and an explicit Japanese subject declaration.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports a revised Japanese passport with a leather cover, starting about August 1938 with number 344501, and sends ten specimens.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2897: Revision of the Japanese Passport Form

subfiles.about: Japanese Foreign Office memorandum requesting that U.S. authorities be advised of changes to Japanese passports and transmitting specimen copies.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Foreign Office memo announcing revised passports from about August 1938, starting with number 344501, with twelve samples.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Japanese Foreign Office Regarding Revised Passport Forms

subfiles.about: State Department circular instruction alerting American diplomatic and consular officers to modifications in Japanese passports (mailing desk copy).
subfiles.summary: Mailing copy of visa instruction No. 2940 on revised Japanese passports from August 1938, stamped June 1938.
subfiles.title: Visa Instruction (Diplomatic Serial No. 2940): Revised Japanese Passports (Mailing Copy)

subfiles.about: Official master copy of circular visa instruction signed by Assistant Secretary Messersmith detailing revisions to Japanese passports.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith (Assistant Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Messersmith's visa instruction No. 2940 tells all consular officers of the revised Japanese passport's leather cover and nationality statement.
subfiles.title: Visa Instruction (Diplomatic Serial No. 2940): Revised Japanese Passports (Official Signed Copy)

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum transmitting copies of Tokyo Despatch No. 2897 and sample Japanese passports to the Secretary of Labor.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State (Cordell Hull / Visa Division)
subfiles.summary: State sends Labor Secretary Frances Perkins copies of Tokyo despatch No. 2897 and two specimen Japanese passports.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Secretary of Labor Transmitting Japanese Passport Samples

subfiles.about: Duplicate file copy of Diplomatic Serial No. 2940 instructing diplomatic and consular officers on the revised Japanese passport format.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith (Assistant Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: File copy of visa instruction No. 2940 on revised Japanese passports starting with number 344501.
subfiles.title: Visa Instruction (Diplomatic Serial No. 2940): Revised Japanese Passports (Duplicate File Copy)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet linking Tokyo Despatch No. 4061 (filed under 800.0128/72) to the Japan decimal file 894.0128.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Tokyo despatch No. 4061 sending sample Japanese passports, filed at 800.0128/72.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 4061 Transmitting Sample Passports

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting sixteen specimen passports across four distinct categories issued by the Japanese government.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Dooman sends sixteen specimen Japanese passports in four classes, in response to a circular requesting samples of foreign passports.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4061: Summary of Foreign Passports - Japan

subfiles.about: American Embassy note requesting up to sixteen specimen passports issued by the Japanese government for comparative study.
subfiles.summary: The Tokyo Embassy asks the Japanese Foreign Ministry for up to sixteen specimen passports, including those for colonies and mandates, for comparative study.
subfiles.title: Embassy Note No. 1333 Requesting Specimen Japanese Passports

subfiles.about: Japanese Foreign Office note detailing passport categories and jurisdictional authorities across Japan proper and imperial territories.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Ministry sends sixteen specimen passports in four classes, explaining that all passports issued within the Empire bear the Foreign Minister's name.
subfiles.title: Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs Note Describing Passport Categories and Imperial Jurisdictions
